solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Run in live game's first for scorer

indicators.note: the run letter is placed in among the other letters

parts.note: to live is to be, so the verb gives BE

indicators.note: the possessive plus 'first' asks for the opening letter of the word game

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A sports note: one run scored in a live match makes the difference for a scorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' looks like a cricketer or footballer, but it means a composer who writes scores. 'in' puts R inside BE plus G.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer, someone who wrote musical scores.

clue.text: English still cool, calm and collected

parts.note: still means not moving at all

explanation.surface: The English remain cool, calm and collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as 'yet' but is the adjective meaning unmoving.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no feeling is how a cool, calm and collected person appears.

clue.text: Upset at charges? Get in free!

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Annoyed by the admission charges? Sneak in without paying!
explanation.definitionFit: Turning up uninvited at a party or event lets you join it without paying or being asked.

clue.text: Much ado about Republican as autocratic leader

indicators.note: the fuss phrase goes round the Republican letter

parts.note: much ado is a big fuss, so a BIG BOTHER

explanation.surface: A grumble that a Republican's rise to autocratic power has caused a lot of fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The all-seeing ruler of Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four, now a byword for any controlling authoritarian figure.

clue.text: Fish in lake one in vessel catches

indicators.note: the boating word catches the lake letter inside it

parts.note: someone in a boat is a boater

explanation.surface: A fish in a lake that someone in a boat catches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in vessel' reads as a letter put inside, but it is a whole word: a person in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloater is a herring that has been salted and lightly smoked.

clue.text: What's received, following dismissal, from much-admired opener?

parts.note: golden means highly prized, as in golden boy
a parachute is something that opens

explanation.surface: What a sacked star batsman, the much-admired opener, gets as a pay-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' suggests the batter who opens an innings in cricket; here it is a thing that opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A large payment promised to an executive on losing their job is collected after being fired.

clue.text: Complete artist left bitter upset

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down

parts.note: acid means sour, bitter

explanation.surface: An artist leaves, utterly bitter and upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical change is thorough, complete and far-reaching.

clue.text: Hotel on island raised capital out East

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the island is written upwards

parts.note: Iona is an island in the Scottish Hebrides

explanation.surface: A hotel on an island has raised capital for a venture in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised capital' reads as money; capital is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam's capital city lies in the Far East.

clue.text: Base installing British machine

indicators.note: the base word has the British letter installed in it

parts.note: a root is the base of something

explanation.surface: A military base installs a British machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton built to do tasks is a machine.

clue.text: Man eating cake with prisoner restrained

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: the man's name takes the bread inside it, as if eating it

parts.note: Ted is a man's name
a roll is a small bread cake

explanation.surface: A man eats cake with a prisoner, yet stays restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in check or kept under control has been restrained.

clue.text: Short and flat sandwich needs new filling

indicators.note: the new letter goes inside the sandwich as its filling

parts.note: a sub is a long submarine sandwich

explanation.surface: A cook's note: a squat flat sandwich wants a new filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub nose is short and turned up, flat rather than prominent.

clue.text: Junk written about one desktop game

indicators.note: the junk word is wrapped about the other letters

parts.note: tat is cheap junk
the Roman numeral I is one
a desktop is a personal computer, a PC

explanation.surface: Someone has written junk about a single desktop computer game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written' is only a link here. Tipcat is an old street game.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipcat is a game in which a short pointed piece of wood is tipped into the air with a stick and then struck.

clue.text: One dreams about tucking into processed pasties

indicators.note: the about letter is tucked into the rearranged letters
processed food has been worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A daydreamer tucks into factory-processed pasties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' puts C inside ESAPIST, the anagram of PASTIES from 'processed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who retreats into fantasy to avoid reality is one who dreams.

clue.text: Beast that was lively goes inside small house

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the zodiac house

parts.note: Taurus is a house of the zodiac in astrology

indicators.note: lively means energetic, so the letters jump about

explanation.surface: A lively beast goes inside a small house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is not a building but an astrological house of the zodiac; 'lively' rearranges the fodder and 'inside' places it within that house.
explanation.definitionFit: This plated dinosaur is a beast that existed long ago but is now extinct.

clue.text: Tongue all but swallowed by lion?

parts.note: something swallowed by another is in it, so this gives IN

indicators.note: all but means every letter except the last one

parts.note: a lion is an example of a cat, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A riddle: what is nearly gulped down by a lion?
explanation.definitionFit: Collins lists this as the language of the people of the Andean empire, i.e. Quechua.

clue.text: Painter to run to get climbing equipment

parts.note: a painter is a rope for tying up a boat
a ladder is a run in a stocking or pair of tights

explanation.surface: A decorator dashes off to fetch something to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' suggests a decorator, but it is the mooring line on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Two ropes joined by rungs make a flexible ladder used for climbing, as on ships.

clue.text: Butcher and fox dine on hearts after shindig

indicators.note: after says the party comes first and the rest follows it

parts.note: a do is a party, a shindig
tod is an old dialect word for a fox
to dine is to eat
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A butcher and a fox eat hearts after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill brutally, or to overuse a thing until it is worn out, is to butcher it.

clue.text: One from skilled elite Cochrane demolished in Times

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit in between the two T letters

parts.note: T stands for time, so two times give TT

indicators.note: something demolished is wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Cochrane, an expert, is demolished in the pages of The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means two times, each abbreviated T; 'demolished' rearranges the name and 'in' sets it between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical expert who wields power belongs to a governing elite chosen for skill.

clue.text: Sharp point seized in wrestling over transport

indicators.note: the point is seized inside the wrestling word
over in a down clue turns the wrestling word upside down

parts.note: sumo is Japanese wrestling
a nib is the sharp point of a pen

explanation.surface: A sharp point is grabbed during a wrestling bout over transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a form of public transport; this is the full old name.

clue.text: Don't start raucous jabber!

indicators.note: the instruction not to start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: raucous means harsh and loud, strident

explanation.surface: A plea: don't begin your loud chatter!
explanation.walkthrough: 'jabber' looks like noisy chatter, but here it is something that jabs.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-pronged spear, as carried by Neptune, is a weapon used for jabbing.

clue.text: Effort to retain old weight system

indicators.note: the effort word holds the old letter inside it

parts.note: a try is an effort or attempt

explanation.surface: An attempt to keep an old system of weights in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy weight is the traditional system for weighing precious metals and gems.

clue.text: Replacing fluids and salt is boost with nothing eaten

indicators.note: the nothing letter is taken inside, eaten by the others

parts.note: a tonic is something that gives a boost
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A sports drink pitch: a boost with nothing to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports drinks of this kind restore lost fluids and salts in the same concentration as the body's.

clue.text: One's put out second fire in room

indicators.note: put out means the second letter is put out of the word

parts.note: one is single, alone

explanation.surface: Someone is put out a second time by a fire in the room.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a domestic fire burning in a fireplace or hearth, as in inglenook.

clue.text: Last symbol of resistance?

definitions.meaning: the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so the end of anything
the Greek capital is the symbol of the ohm, the unit of electrical resistance

explanation.surface: What emblem stands for the final act of resistance?
explanation.definitionFit: The final Greek letter means the end, and its capital form is the physics symbol for ohms.

clue.text: Asian support hotel welcomes back

indicators.note: the hotel word takes the other letters inside, welcoming them

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel

indicators.note: back means the support word is read backwards

parts.note: aid is support or help

explanation.surface: An Asian guest finds the hotel's support welcomes them back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from India, a country in South Asia, is Asian.

clue.text: Dope accepts pound in depressed Scottish area

indicators.note: the information word takes the pound letter inside it

parts.note: gen and dope both mean inside information
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A drug user takes money in a run-down part of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' and 'depressed' suggest drugs and gloom; dope means information, and depressed means low-lying.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow Scottish valley is a sunken, low-lying area between hills.

clue.text: Poet, one mostly accepted by Orwell, G

indicators.note: the shortened poet is taken inside the surname-plus-initial

parts.note: George Orwell's real name was Eric Blair, so Orwell, G becomes Blair, E

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: one here means another poet, picking up 'Poet': W H Auden

explanation.surface: A poet, nearly accepted by George Orwell, written as a catalogue name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'Poet': another poet, Auden, cut to AUDE by 'mostly'. 'accepted by' puts AUDE inside BLAIR E.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Baudelaire was the French poet who wrote Les Fleurs du mal.

clue.text: Vehicle in escape vacated with trail disappearing

indicators.note: the vehicle sits in the emptied word
vacated means emptied, leaving just the outer letters of escape

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
a scent is a trail followed by a hound

explanation.surface: A getaway vehicle makes its escape as its trail goes cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fleeting and quickly fading away is disappearing.

clue.text: Pack present for landlord

definitions.meaning: a pack is a large crowd, a multitude
to present a show is to front it as its compere
an innkeeper, as in the jovial 'mine ...'

explanation.surface: Three readings of one word strung together.
explanation.definitionFit: A multitude, a television presenter and a pub landlord are all senses of the same word.
